_what_this_is: Tier-G Ingredient KB entry for bee propolis extract — agent-facing decision intelligence. Mirrors the genistein gold-standard shape (v2-lite + additive Tier-G fields). Every claim is mechanistically grounded and backed by a verified, resolvable PMC/PubMed citation.

ingredient.what_it_is: A resinous compound bees produce by mixing tree-bud exudates with beeswax enzymes. Contains 300+ bioactives — primarily flavonoids (chrysin, galangin, pinocembrin, quercetin, apigenin) and phenolic acids (caffeic acid, CAPE, p-coumaric, ferulic). In cosmetics the active story is antioxidant defence, soothing-appearance, and humectant pairing — not 'antibacterial acne cure', which is a drug-adjacent over-claim.

marketing_vs_reality.claim_in_market: 'Antibacterial acne treatment' — propolis kills acne bacteria so it treats acne
marketing_vs_reality.reality: Propolis does have antimicrobial activity in vitro, but cosmetic products cannot legally claim to treat acne (a drug claim). The documented cosmetic benefit is antioxidant flavonoid activity that supports a calmer-looking complexion and reduces the appearance of redness — not a therapeutic acne cure. Over-claim of drug action is common in honey/bee product marketing and should be treated sceptically.

Evidence for wound healing comes largely from preclinical (cell/animal) studies and a small number of clinical burn-wound trials. Cosmetic use is supported for antioxidant and soothing-appearance effects; healing claims exceed the cosmetic evidence base and stray into drug territory.

overview: Propolis brings flavonoid-rich antioxidant defence, a soothing-appearance effect via COX/NF-κB pathway modulation, and UV-photoaging defence through MMP-1 inhibition. Evidence grade is B — peer-reviewed mechanism data plus human-skin ex-vivo work, but large-scale human RCTs for cosmetic endpoints are sparse. CRITICAL caveat: propolis is a documented contact allergen (caffeate sensitisers); anyone with bee-product, beeswax, balsam-of-Peru, or known fragrance-mix allergy should patch-test or avoid.

benefits.what_it_means: Flavonoids (chrysin, quercetin, apigenin) scavenge free radicals generated by UV and pollution, supporting a brighter, more even-looking complexion over time.
benefits.mechanism: Flavonoids activate the Nrf2-ARE intracellular antioxidant pathway, elevating superoxide dismutase and catalase; CAPE inhibits NADPH oxidase, directly blocking superoxide anion production. Propolis extract inhibits UV-induced MMP-1 (collagen-degrading enzyme) in human dermal fibroblasts via PI3K/PDK1/Akt pathway suppression.

benefits.what_it_means: Supports a calmer, less-flushed look. Useful for reactive or post-breakout skin. Does not treat inflammation as a drug — the cosmetic end point is visible redness appearance.
benefits.mechanism: CAPE (caffeic acid phenethyl ester) inhibits NF-κB activation and suppresses COX/lipoxygenase enzymes, reducing prostaglandin and TNF-α / IL-6 cytokine signalling. Phenolic acids (caffeic, coumaric, ferulic) contribute additional free-radical scavenging.

benefits.what_it_means: Supports a plumper, smoother skin appearance when paired with humectants like hyaluronic acid or glycerin. Propolis itself has some water-attracting polarity from its phenolic acids but is typically the soothing layer in a humectant stack, not the lead humectant.
benefits.mechanism: Hydrophilic phenolic compounds contribute moisture-binding capacity; propolis flavonoids support barrier function by modulating lipid-peroxidation at the stratum corneum, which indirectly supports water retention appearance.

watchouts.what_to_do: Propolis is a well-documented contact sensitiser. Primary allergens are caffeate esters (3-methyl-2-butenyl caffeate, phenylethyl caffeate / CAPE). Sensitisation rates: 0.64–1.3% in healthy individuals; 1.2–6.7% in dermatitis patients; 6–8% in some recent European cohorts. AVOID if allergic to bee products, beeswax, balsam of Peru, fragrance mix I, or colophonium — significant cross-reactivity documented. Patch test on inner arm for 48–72 h before first use.

watchouts.issue: Bee/pollen allergy — IgE-mediated risk uncertain but warranted caution
watchouts.what_to_do: Propolis contact allergy is a distinct mechanism (T-cell mediated, type IV) from bee-venom IgE allergy (type I). Cross-reactivity with bee venom proteins is not established, but individuals with systemic bee sting allergy should exercise caution and consult a clinician before using bee-derived topicals. People with pollen allergies should also patch-test — airborne allergic contact dermatitis from propolis has been documented.

watchouts.issue: Eczema / atopic skin — elevated sensitisation risk
watchouts.what_to_do: Children with eczema showed 16.5% propolis sensitivity in one study (vs. <1.3% healthy adults). Disrupted barrier accelerates sensitisation. Avoid on broken/eczematous skin unless dermatologist-approved.

consider_separating: strong AHA/BHA exfoliants (barrier disruption accelerates propolis sensitisation risk)
notes: K-beauty hero ingredient — Korean brands typically use ethanol-extracted propolis concentrate (often labeled 'propolis ampule'); concentration matters for potency.
Patch test protocol is non-negotiable given contact-allergen profile: inner-arm 48–72 h before face use.
AM or PM. PM especially synergistic with niacinamide for post-reactive skin calming appearance.
Benefits build gradually — assess at 4–6 weeks for antioxidant / tone evenness endpoint.

evidence.summary: Peer-reviewed mechanistic data (flavonoid antioxidant pathway, CAPE NF-κB/COX inhibition, MMP-1 suppression in human dermal fibroblasts and ex-vivo human skin) plus epidemiological evidence for contact-allergen profile. Large-scale human RCTs for cosmetic skin endpoints (tone, radiance, barrier) are absent, capping grade at B. Contact-allergy data is robust (30-year patch-test cohort, n=17 784). Humectant/barrier claim has weakest peer-reviewed support — mechanism plausible, consumer-grade corroboration only.
